open_questions/0.rationale: What is established is that the enzyme is missing from lesional epidermis and hair follicles, and that the eruption occurs in a minority of patients, sometimes decades after the muscle phenotype. What is not established is the step between the two. Keratinocytes are highly glycolytic, but no study has shown that a keratinocyte ATP or redox deficit drives the inflammatory phenotype, and the pustular cases were specifically reported as not carrying IL36RN variants, which excludes the obvious alternative explanation of coincidental generalised pustular psoriasis. The seasonal pattern — flares in warm months, remission in autumn — is unexplained by any current model.

open_questions/1.rationale: Four patients from two families carrying the same 20-base-pair deletion differed markedly in severity, and the group that reported them found threefold higher muscle glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase activity in the mildly affected patients. That is a plausible modifier and it is the only one proposed, but it rests on four patients and a correlation, with no genetic variant identified in GPD1 or elsewhere and no independent replication in the thirty years since. The alternative offered by the same group — that severity tracks muscle oxidative capacity — has the same evidential standing, and the two have never been separated.

evidence.snippet: Two missense mutations (C356R and C356G) of GDD1 were identified in the two families with GDD (the original Japanese family and a new African American family), and both missense mutations occur at the cysteine residue at amino acid 356, which is evolutionarily conserved among human, mouse, zebrafish, fruit fly, and mosquito.
evidence.explanation: The founding gene-identification study, establishing GDD1/ANO5 missense change at a single conserved cysteine as the cause of GDD.

evidence.snippet: It appears that all GDD mutations known so far locate in an extracellular domain following the first transmembrane domain or in the 4th putative transmembrane domain.
evidence.explanation: Documents the tight positional clustering of GDD alleles, which is difficult to reconcile with simple haploinsufficiency.

steps/1.description: GDD is caused by a heterozygous missense variant in ANO5 (TMEM16E), the gene originally designated GDD1. The reported alleles are strikingly clustered: the founding Japanese and African American families carried substitutions at the evolutionarily conserved cysteine 356 (p.Cys356Arg, p.Cys356Gly, and later p.Cys356Tyr), and subsequent families added p.Cys360Tyr, p.Arg215Gly, p.Ser500Phe, p.Thr513Ile and p.Gly518Glu. All map either to the extracellular loop following the first transmembrane domain or to the fourth putative transmembrane domain, which is what makes a simple gene-dosage explanation implausible: a haploinsufficiency mechanism would tolerate nonsense and frameshift alleles anywhere in the gene, and those alleles instead produce a recessive myopathy.

evidence.snippet: While the activity of wild-type TMEM16E depended on elevated cytosolic Ca2+ levels, a mutant form carrying the GDD-causing T513I substitution showed PLS and large time-dependent ion currents even at low cytosolic Ca2+ concentrations.
evidence.explanation: Direct demonstration that a GDD allele uncouples TMEM16E scrambling from its normal calcium requirement - constitutive activity, not absent activity.

evidence.snippet: Our results collectively demonstrate that, on the level of protein function, MD mutations are associated to loss-of-function and GDD mutations to gain-of-function phenotypes, confirming conjectures made on the basis of inheritance modes.
evidence.explanation: The head-to-head comparison establishing the allelic dichotomy at the level of protein function, and explicitly grounding it in the opposite inheritance modes.

evidence.snippet: Cellular localization to the endoplasmic reticulum suggests a role for GDD1 in the regulation of intracellular calcium homeostasis.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the ER localization that constrains where the scrambling defect can act; the calcium-regulation role is inferred rather than measured here, hence PARTIAL.

steps/2.description: ANO5 encodes TMEM16E/anoctamin-5, a member of the TMEM16 family that behaves as a calcium-activated phospholipid scramblase and a poorly selective ion conduit, and that localizes predominantly to the endoplasmic reticulum rather than the plasma membrane. In heterologous expression, the GDD-associated p.Thr513Ile protein scrambles phospholipid and carries large currents even at very low cytosolic calcium, i.e. it is uncoupled from its normal calcium gating rather than inactivated. When GDD alleles and muscular-dystrophy alleles were compared side by side in the same assay system, they moved in opposite directions - GDD towards gain of function, muscular dystrophy towards loss of function. This is the node at which the two ANO5 diseases separate, and it is why bone disease is not simply "less ANO5".

evidence.snippet: Further analysis revealed that Ano5 deficiency upregulated the expression of ATG9A, and silencing ATG9A significantly reduced both autophagy and osteogenic activity in Ano5-/- mCOBs.
evidence.explanation: Establishes ATG9A-dependent autophagy as a required intermediate for the excess osteogenesis, with the silencing experiment supplying the causal direction.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, ANO5 mutation promoted the phosphorylation of AMPK, the classical sensor of energy metabolism.
evidence.explanation: Places AMPK activation downstream of a genotype-matched GDD knock-in allele (p.Cys360Tyr), not merely of Ano5 loss.

evidence.snippet: In this study, we found that Ano5 deficiency notably inhibited miR-34c-5p expression. Krüppel-Like Factor 4 (Klf4), a target gene of miR-34c-5p confirmed by dual luciferase reporter assay, was up-regulated in Ano5-/- mCOBs, accompanied by activated downstream canonical Wnt/β-catenin signaling and increased expression of β-catenin.
evidence.explanation: Supplies the miR-34c-5p/KLF4/beta-catenin arm with a validated target relationship.

evidence.snippet: Additionally, Ano5 Cys360Tyr mutation down-regulated the Akt phosphorylation level in osteoblast.
evidence.explanation: The Akt arm, again in the genotype-matched knock-in. Note the direction: Akt is DECREASED, and it is Akt re-activation that suppresses the excess mineralization.

steps/3.description:
The osteoblast-side intermediate between the ANO5 defect and the remodelling imbalance. Four convergent mouse studies identify signalling routes by which perturbed ANO5 drives excess bone formation: AMPK phosphorylation rises and accelerates glycolysis and PGC1a-dependent mitochondrial respiration; AMPK in turn upregulates ATG9A and activates autophagy, which is required for the excess osteogenesis; miR-34c-5p falls, de-repressing KLF4 and activating canonical Wnt/beta-catenin; and Akt phosphorylation falls, with Akt re-activation suppressing mineralization. Each arm has a pharmacological or genetic rescue.
READ THE GENOTYPES BEFORE TRANSFERRING ANY OF THIS TO HUMAN GDD. The AMPK and Akt arms come from the Ano5 p.Cys360Tyr knock-in, which carries an actual human GDD allele. The autophagy/ATG9A, miR-34c-5p/KLF4 and NF-kB arms come from Ano5-null mice - a genotype that in humans causes myopathy, not bone disease. So this node is better evidenced than the bare "unknown intermediates" it replaces, but it is not thereby established for human GDD, and the two model classes are not interchangeable. See `gdd_mouse_model_mismatch`.

evidence.snippet: RANKL-induced early signaling pathways were suppressed in Ano5-/- osteoclasts and Ano5 knockdown RAW264.7 cells. Moreover, the inhibitory effects of NF-κB signalling pathway on osteoclastogenesis were partially attenuated with NF-κB signalling activator.
evidence.explanation: Establishes suppressed RANKL/NF-kB signalling as the osteoclast intermediate, with partial pharmacological reversal supplying the causal direction.

evidence.snippet: In addition, the endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS) response was significantly enhanced in Ano5-/- osteoclasts, possibly because of calcium dyshomeostasis, which leading to the increased proportion of apoptotic osteoclasts via the activation of the C/EBP homologous protein (CHOP) signalling pathway
evidence.explanation: Supplies the ER-stress/CHOP apoptosis arm and ties it back to calcium dyshomeostasis, connecting this node to the upstream ER calcium claim.

evidence.snippet: Akt activation promoted the generation of TRAP-positive multinucleated osteoclasts and the formation of actin rings in Ano5 KI/KI BMMs cultures
evidence.explanation: The Akt arm in the genotype-matched knock-in, with rescue of both multinucleation and the actin ring defect noted elsewhere in this entry.

steps/4.description:
The osteoclast-side intermediate. Perturbed ANO5 suppresses RANKL-induced early signalling and the NF-kB pathway, reducing NFATc1, c-Fos and the osteoclast effector programme and leaving disrupted actin rings with impaired mineral resorption. Separately, calcium dyshomeostasis in Ano5-null osteoclasts drives an overactivated endoplasmic-reticulum stress response and CHOP-mediated apoptosis, so osteoclasts are both under-differentiated and actively lost. Akt is the third arm: it is reduced in the knock-in, and the Akt activator SC79 restores multinucleated osteoclast formation.
The same genotype caveat as the osteoblast node applies - the NF-kB and ER-stress arms are null-mouse work.

evidence.snippet: After Ano5 gene knock-down with shRNA in MC3T3-E1 osteoblast precursors we saw elevated expression of osteoblast-related genes such as Col1a1, osteocalcin, osterix and Runx2 as well as increased mineral nodule formation in differentiating cells.
evidence.explanation: Links ANO5 perturbation to an osteoblast differentiation and mineralization phenotype in an osteoblast precursor line.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, Ano5-mediated Akt phosphorylation resulted in nuclear factor of activated T-cells c1 (NFATc1) activation, indicating that Ano5 regulates osteoclast differentiation through activation of the Akt-NFATc1 signaling pathway.
evidence.explanation: Places ANO5 in the RANKL-Akt-NFATc1 osteoclast differentiation axis, the osteoclast arm of the remodelling imbalance.

evidence.snippet: Downregulation of Ano5 expression did not affect osteoblast differentiation and mineralization, while ectopic expression of Ano5 significantly enhanced receptor activator of nuclear factor kappa B ligand (RANKL)-induced osteoclast differentiation.
evidence.explanation: A directly contrary result on the osteoblast arm - no effect, where another system reported an increase - which is why the osteoblast process carries DYSREGULATED rather than a direction. Also shows the osteoclast effect runs the opposite way from the knock-in mouse.

steps/5.description: ANO5 is expressed in osteoblasts and periodontal ligament cells, and manipulating it in cell culture perturbs both arms of bone remodelling. Knockdown in osteoblast precursors raises osteoblast marker expression and mineral nodule formation, while ANO5 supports RANKL-driven osteoclast differentiation through Akt-NFATc1 signalling and its loss impairs osteoclastogenesis and actin-ring formation. The direction of effect is not consistent across systems - which is itself informative, and is the reason the cellular arm is curated as a hypothesis-tagged step rather than a settled mechanism. Both processes therefore carry `modifier: DYSREGULATED` rather than a direction: knockdown in MC3T3-E1 precursors increased osteoblast markers and mineralization, ANO5 downregulation in another system did not affect osteoblast differentiation at all, and the Ano5-null osteoblasts of a third study showed decreased indices. Asserting INCREASED here would pick a winner among three published directions.

evidence.snippet: We thereby identified increased trabecular bone mass accompanied by elevated serum markers of bone formation and bone resorption.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the high-turnover character of the skeletal phenotype in a genetically confirmed GDD patient.

evidence.snippet: The high turnover bone pathology was further confirmed through the analysis of an iliac crest biopsy, where osteoblast and osteoclast indices were remarkably increased.
evidence.explanation: Histomorphometric confirmation that both cell lineages are hyperactive, tying the tissue phenotype back to the cellular node.

steps/6.description: Full osteological assessment of a GDD patient carrying p.Ser500Phe showed increased trabecular bone mass with elevated serum markers of both bone formation and bone resorption, and an iliac crest biopsy with markedly increased osteoblast and osteoclast indices. GDD is therefore not a low-turnover sclerosing disease: bone is being both laid down and resorbed faster than normal, and the resulting tissue is sclerotic in the diaphyses yet mechanically inadequate. Elevated serum alkaline phosphatase is the usual laboratory correlate of this high-turnover presentation, but it is not universal across GDD: the osteopenic sub-entity has been reported with low bone-formation markers, and individual patients with normal ALP are documented.

evidence.snippet: Results showed that all three patients harbored the heterozygous mutation c.1067G > A (p.Cys356Tyr) in the ANO5 gene.
evidence.explanation: Ties the recurrent GDD allele to expansile multi-quadrant gnathic fibro-osseous disease, supporting a shared lesion biology.

evidence.snippet: Our findings indicate that FGC may be an atypical variant of GDD, providing evidence for the feasibility of ANO5 gene testing as an auxiliary diagnostic method for complex cases with multiple quadrants.
evidence.explanation: Supports treating familial gigantiform cementoma as within the GDD spectrum rather than as a differential to be excluded.

steps/7.description: The gnathic component of GDD is a multi-quadrant fibro-osseous lesion of the mandible and maxilla - cementum-like calcified deposits scattered in a fibroblastic stroma - that expands, deforms the face, and frequently becomes secondarily infected. It has been variously reported as florid cemento-osseous dysplasia, cemento-ossifying fibroma, or familial gigantiform cementoma, and ANO5 p.Cys356Tyr has since been found in familial gigantiform cementoma kindreds, suggesting that entity is an atypical variant of GDD rather than a separate disease. Notably, osteosclerosis - the hallmark of the long-bone lesion - is not a feature of the jaw lesion, so the two components of GDD are not the same pathology in two places.

evidence.snippet: One Caucasian family with seven affected members exhibited frequent bone fractures and florid osseous dysplasia (p.Cys356Tyr), while one Chinese family with two affected members suffered from cementoma and purulent osteomyelitis (p.Cys360Tyr).
evidence.explanation: Documents the co-occurrence of fractures with gnathic fibro-osseous disease in genotyped families.

evidence.snippet: Gnathodiaphyseal dysplasia (GDD) is a rare skeletal syndrome that involves an osteopetrosis-like sclerosis of the long bones and fibrous dysplasia-like cemento-osseous lesions of the jawbone.
evidence.explanation: Substantiates the sclerosis half of this node, which the fracture-focused evidence above does not address.

evidence.snippet: his radiographs showed gross thickening of the diaphyseal cortices of long bones with narrow medullary canals
evidence.explanation: Human radiographic evidence for the cortical-thickening component of this node.

steps/8.description: The extragnathic skeletal phenotype: sclerosis and cortical thickening of the diaphyses of the tubular bones, bowing of the lower limbs, and recurrent fractures that typically begin around puberty but may present prenatally as bone bowing. The combination of radiographically dense bone with a high fracture rate is the feature that historically caused GDD to be misfiled as osteogenesis imperfecta.

evidence.snippet: first described in a large Japanese family including 21 patients exhibiting frequent bone fractures in adolescence and purulent osteomyelitis of the jaws during adult life
evidence.explanation: Establishes the age-staged pattern of adolescent fractures followed by adult jaw osteomyelitis in the founding kindred.

steps/9.description: Jaw lesions enlarge through adolescence and adult life, producing maxillofacial deformity and malocclusion that may require orthognathic or reconstructive surgery, and are susceptible to purulent osteomyelitis. This was a defining feature of the original Japanese kindred.

edges/1.description: The missense substitution acts on the protein's own transport behaviour; this is the step demonstrated directly in heterologous expression.

edges/2.description: Route to the osteoblast arm. Candidate intermediates are now identified in mouse models, but the step from altered TMEM16E scrambling to those signalling changes has not been demonstrated in patient bone.

edges/3.description: Route to the osteoclast arm, evidenced in the same model systems and subject to the same caveat.

edges/4.description: These signalling changes are what the differentiation phenotype is measured as; each arm's rescue reverses the osteogenic excess.

edges/5.description: Reduced osteoclast differentiation and increased osteoclast apoptosis are the resorption-side half of the remodelling imbalance.

edges/6.description: A coordinated disturbance of osteoblast and osteoclast behaviour is what produces the paradoxical combination of sclerotic, thickened bone that nevertheless fractures. This edge is claimed by BOTH mechanistic hypotheses, and that is the point: they disagree about the SIGN of the remodelling change - the gain-of-function model predicts increased indices and high bone mass, the sub-entity model predicts decreased indices and osteopenia for loss-of-function alleles - while agreeing that the cellular imbalance is what produces the skeletal phenotype.

edges/7.description: The jaw-selective step. Why a systemically expressed ER scramblase produces focal, expansile fibro-osseous masses confined to the gnathic skeleton is unexplained; see the knowledge-gap discussion. The expanding cell population on that node is deliberately left as free text rather than bound to CL:0000061 cementoblast, because which lineage expands is precisely what `gdd_jaw_selectivity_gap` records as untested.

edges/8.description: Accelerated, poorly coordinated remodelling yields thickened sclerotic diaphyses whose material quality does not match their apparent density.

edges/9.description: Expansile avascular fibro-osseous masses in tooth-bearing bone deform the face and provide a nidus for purulent infection.

evidence.snippet: By linkage analysis of a large Japanese family with GDD, we previously mapped the GDD locus to chromosome 11p14.3-15.1.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the GDD locus subsequently shown to contain ANO5.

evidence.snippet: Mutations in the human TMEM16E/ANO5 gene are causative for gnathodiaphyseal dysplasia (GDD), a rare bone malformation and fragility disorder, and for two types of muscular dystrophy (MD).
evidence.explanation: States the two-disease allelic architecture of ANO5 that this entry contrasts against the LGMD entry.

evidence.snippet: absent in dbSNP, 1000Genomes, the Exome Variant Server (~6500 exomes) and the ExAC database
evidence.explanation: Population-database absence of the GDD alleles, supporting pathogenicity and relevant to the allelic contrast: ANO5 truncating alleles are by comparison common enough in the population to sustain a recessive disease.

genes/0.notes: ANO5 (TMEM16E; originally GDD1) at 11p14.3-15.1 is the sole gene known to cause GDD. The GDD allele class is heterozygous missense; the same gene's biallelic truncating and loss-of-function alleles cause limb-girdle muscular dystrophy R12 and Miyoshi-like distal myopathy, curated in Autosomal_Recessive_Limb-Girdle_Muscular_Dystrophy. Obligate heterozygous carriers of those null alleles - the parents of affected LGMDR12 individuals - are not reported to develop the GDD skeletal phenotype, which is the clinical observation that argues against haploinsufficiency as the GDD mechanism.

evidence.snippet: We assessed his response to a total of 7 pamidronate infusions commencing at age 15months
evidence.explanation: Documents pamidronate exposure in a GDD patient. PARTIAL because it is a single case and the snippet records that a response was assessed, not that a particular benefit was established.

evidence.snippet: The osteopenia is being treated with pamidronate.
evidence.explanation: A second, independent report of pamidronate use, and notably in an OSTEOPENIC patient - the sub-entity for which an antiresorptive is directionally appropriate.

treatments/0.description:
Intravenous pamidronate has been given to GDD patients with low bone mass and fractures. The evidence is case-level - a child treated with seven infusions from 15 months of age, and a separate patient whose osteopenia was managed with pamidronate - and no controlled data exist.
The mechanistic caveat is the important part and follows directly from the sub-entity split this entry curates. An antiresorptive suppresses bone resorption, which is coherent for the low-bone-mass, osteopenic GDD sub-entity, but is the wrong direction for the high-turnover osteosclerotic sub-entity, where trabecular bone mass is already increased. Bone mass and turnover markers should therefore be established before an antiresorptive is chosen, rather than inferring from the diagnosis alone.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Suppresses the osteoclastic resorption arm of the remodelling imbalance. Directionally appropriate only for the low-bone-mass sub-entity.

evidence.snippet: Osteoanabolic treatment of parathyroid hormone was effective in enhancing bone strength in Ano5 KO mice.
evidence.explanation: Model-organism evidence only, in a null genotype unlike human GDD, hence PARTIAL and explicitly not a treatment recommendation.

treatments/1.description:
Parathyroid hormone enhanced bone strength in Ano5-knockout mice. This is a mouse result in a genotype that does not correspond to human GDD, and no human GDD patient has been reported treated with an osteoanabolic. It is curated because it is the only pharmacological rescue reported for any ANO5 bone model, and because it is the directional complement of the bisphosphonate entry: osteoanabolic for low bone mass, antiresorptive for high turnover. This is NOT a clinical recommendation.
No `therapeutic_agent` is bound, deliberately. The source says "parathyroid hormone" without naming an analogue. Teriparatide has both CHEBI and NCIT identities and would be the obvious binding, but it is specifically PTH 1-34, and asserting it would attribute an agent the paper does not specify; neither ontology offers a plain "parathyroid hormone" therapeutic term. Left unbound rather than made precise beyond the evidence.

treatments/1/targets/0.description: Shifts the remodelling balance towards formation; demonstrated only in the low-bone-mass null mouse.

evidence.snippet: He was treated with LeFort 1 advancement and Bilateral Sagittal Split Osteotomy of the mandible with setback procedures. No complications were seen and 2-year follow-up showed stable dental occlusion.
evidence.explanation: Documents the orthognathic procedure and its two-year outcome in a GDD patient.

evidence.snippet: Other procedures are possible, but more research is needed to develop best practices for this disorder.
evidence.explanation: The authors' own statement that the surgical evidence base is not yet sufficient to define standard management.

treatments/2.description: Surgical management of the expansile gnathic lesions and the resulting malocclusion and facial deformity. Orthognathic surgery (Le Fort I advancement with bilateral sagittal split osteotomy) has been performed safely in a GDD patient with stable two-year occlusal follow-up, but the evidence base is single case reports and best practices are not established. This is anatomical correction, not disease modification; no therapy targeting the ANO5 mechanism exists.

treatments/2/targets/0.description: Alters the anatomical outcome node - the deformity and malocclusion produced by the jaw lesions - without acting on any upstream mechanism node.

evidence.snippet: Internal fixation with the Ender nail was effective for the tubular bone with deformity. Callus formation was observed without delay.
evidence.explanation: Reports the outcome of operative fixation in a GDD diaphyseal fracture, including the observation that callus formation was not delayed - relevant because sclerotic GDD bone might be expected to heal poorly.

evidence.snippet: This is the first report describing the treatment of fracture in an adult patient with gnathodiaphyseal dysplasia.
evidence.explanation: Establishes how thin the evidence base is - a single adult case at the time of publication - which is why this treatment is not presented as standard practice.

treatments/3.description: Operative fixation of pathological diaphyseal fractures. Sclerotic, thickened cortices make instrumentation technically demanding, and the reported experience is case-level.

treatments/3/targets/0.description: Symptomatic management of the fracture burden at the outcome node; it does not act on the ANO5 mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Previous studies have demonstrated that TMEM16E/ANO5 is a Ca2+ -activated phospholipid scramblase and that the mutation c.1538C>T (p.Thr513Ile) causing GDD leads to a gain-of-function phenotype.
evidence.explanation: States the gain-of-function characterization that this hypothesis group is built on.

evidence.snippet: GDD is a rare but frequently inherited cause of bone fragility and jaw lesions characterized by a gain-of-function variant within the ANO5 gene.
evidence.explanation: Shows the gain-of-function reading has been adopted as the working model in the contemporary clinical literature. Classified OTHER rather than HUMAN_CLINICAL because the sentence is a literature-review characterization, not an observation the authors made in their own patients.

hypotheses/0.description: The prevailing model: heterozygous GDD missense alleles confer constitutive, calcium-independent phospholipid scrambling on TMEM16E, and that aberrant activity - not a shortfall of ANO5 - disturbs bone-cell behaviour. Its two supports are the dominant inheritance with a restricted missense spectrum, and the head-to-head functional comparison showing GDD and muscular-dystrophy alleles moving in opposite directions in the same assay. Its weakness is that the step from scrambling to a bone lesion, and above all to a jaw-restricted lesion, has not been demonstrated in bone tissue.

evidence.snippet: Overall, our results suggest the existence of GDD-sub-entities with high and low BMD phenotypes due to different GOF and LOF mutations and functions.
evidence.explanation: The authors' explicit statement of the two-sub-entity model that this hypothesis group records.

evidence.snippet: Thus, our results suggest that ANO5 is dosage-sensitive and that LOF of the TMEM16E protein caused by the heterozygous ANO5 mutation in one allele is partly compensated by another normally functional allele.
evidence.explanation: Supplies the dosage-sensitivity argument that lets a partial-loss-of-function allele be dominant without implying that a full null allele would be.

evidence.snippet: Homozygous Ano5 knockout mice (Ano5-/-) replicate some typical traits of human GDD including massive jawbones, bowing tibia, sclerosis and cortical thickening of femoral and tibial diaphyses.
evidence.explanation: A pure loss-of-function genotype reproducing GDD-like bone traits, which is the central difficulty for a strict gain-of-function-only account.

evidence.snippet: We found a causative de novo ANO5 frameshift insertion mutation (p.L370_A371insDYWRLNSTCL) in a GDD family with osteopenia, accompanied by a decrease in TMEM16E expression
evidence.explanation: Reports a GDD family whose allele is not a canonical missense change and is associated with reduced TMEM16E, supporting a reduced-activity route.

evidence.snippet: In vitro studies overexpressing GDD mutations (p.Cys356Tyr and p.Cys360Tyr) showed significantly reduced ANO5 protein.
evidence.explanation: Shows canonical GDD missense alleles reduce steady-state protein, a partial bridge between the two models rather than a decisive result for either. Note the measurement is made in an overexpression system, as the snippet itself states, so it does not establish the protein level in patient bone.

evidence.snippet: The authors also noticed that calvaria-derived Ano5−/− and Ano5KI/KI osteoblasts show increased mineralization and osteoblastogenesis, which partly contradicts our conclusions
evidence.explanation: The authors' own acknowledgement that the increased osteoblastogenesis seen in Ano5-deficient osteoblasts runs against the decreased-indices arm of their sub-entity model. Recorded as REFUTE so the contradiction is visible in the entry rather than only in the prose.

hypotheses/1.description: A reading that does not compete with the gain-of-function model so much as subsume it, and that changes what a curator should record about bone mass. Li et al. propose that GDD comprises two sub-entities assigned by variant class rather than by clinical convention: gain-of-function alleles produce a HIGH-bone-mass phenotype through hyperactive phospholipid scrambling with increased osteoblast and osteoclast indices, while loss-of-function alleles produce a LOW-bone-mass, osteopenic phenotype through impaired calcium oscillations with decreased indices. The supporting observations are that Ano5-knockout mice replicate several cardinal GDD traits, and that a GDD family carrying a frameshift insertion with reduced TMEM16E presented with osteopenia rather than osteosclerosis. One frequently cited finding is NOT support for this model and should not be listed as such: reduced ANO5 in osteoblast precursors INCREASES osteoblastogenesis and mineralization, which runs opposite to the decreased-indices arm proposed here - Li et al. name that result themselves as partly contradicting their own conclusions. Li et al. further argue ANO5 is dosage-sensitive and that their heterozygous frameshift causes only PARTIAL loss of function, partly compensated by the normal allele - which is how a reduced-activity allele can be dominant without being a simple haploinsufficiency. The practical curation consequence is that this entry deliberately does NOT put a single INCREASED or DECREASED modifier on bone mineral density, because either would be wrong for one of the two sub-entities.

open_questions/0.rationale: This is the central unexplained feature of GDD and the reason the causal edge into the jaw lesion node is marked INDIRECT_UNKNOWN_INTERMEDIATES rather than DIRECT. The gnathic and extragnathic lesions are not the same pathology in two locations - jaw lesions are fibro-osseous and specifically lack the osteosclerosis that defines the long-bone lesion - so the disorder needs an account of tissue selectivity, not merely of bone-cell dysfunction. Candidate explanations include a neural-crest-derived versus mesoderm-derived skeletal origin, the distinct periodontal-ligament and cementoblast populations of the gnathic skeleton (ANO5 is expressed in periodontal ligament cells), and the continuous remodelling demand of tooth-bearing bone. None has been tested. Filling this gap with a plausible-sounding chain would misrepresent the state of the evidence.

evidence.snippet: Here we generated Ano5-knockout (KO) mice using a CRISPR/Cas 9 approach to study loss of function aspects of GDD mutations.
evidence.explanation: Frames the loss-of-function investigation whose positive skeletal result is the main tension with the gain-of-function model.

open_questions/1.rationale: The gain-of-function reading rests on strong but indirect grounds - dominant inheritance with a clustered missense spectrum, plus heterologous-expression assays in HEK293 cells showing GDD and muscular-dystrophy alleles moving in opposite directions. Three findings sit awkwardly with it. First, Ano5-knockout mice reproduce several cardinal GDD traits, which a strict gain-of-function model does not predict. Second, canonical GDD missense alleles reduce steady-state ANO5 protein in overexpression studies, so they are not purely hyperactive. Third, a GDD family has been reported with a frameshift insertion and reduced TMEM16E expression. The observation that obligate heterozygous null carriers of LGMDR12 alleles are not reported with bone disease remains the strongest argument against simple haploinsufficiency, but it is an argument from absence in a population that has not been systematically skeletally phenotyped, and that limitation should be stated rather than glossed.

evidence.snippet: This report described the coexistence of muscle and bone phenotypes in the same patients with ANO5-related disorder.
evidence.explanation: Documents the coexistence directly, which is what makes the dichotomy a curated question rather than a settled fact.

evidence.snippet: Our data challenge recent results that suggested complete dichotomy of these phenotypes and the proposed loss-of-function and gain-of-function mechanisms for the skeletal and muscle phenotypes, respectively.
evidence.explanation: The authors' explicit statement that they are challenging the dichotomy this entry otherwise adopts as its organizing frame. Reader caution, since the quote is reproduced verbatim and must not be altered: the trailing "respectively" pairs loss-of-function with the SKELETAL phenotype and gain-of-function with the MUSCLE phenotype, which is the reverse of the assignment made everywhere else in this entry and in the functional literature (PMID:29124309, PMID:32112655, and this paper's own discussion). Treat the sentence as evidence that the dichotomy is being challenged, not as a source for which direction goes with which tissue.

open_questions/2.rationale: The clean dichotomy - dominant missense to bone, recessive null to muscle - is the framing that motivates this entry, and it is largely right, but it is not absolute and the entry should not assert more than the literature supports. An 11-member kindred carrying p.Thr513Ile showed recurrent rhabdomyolysis, muscle cramps, hyperCKemia and muscle hypertrophy alongside the mandibular cemento-osseous lesions, and the authors explicitly framed this as a challenge to the proposed dichotomy. If a single dominant allele can produce both tissue phenotypes, then allele class and tissue are not in one-to-one correspondence, and the gain-of-function versus loss-of-function assignment explains the inheritance pattern better than it explains the tissue distribution.

evidence.snippet: These mice did not display alterations of skeletal microarchitecture or mandible morphology.
evidence.explanation: The negative knock-in result: the murine equivalent of a human GDD allele produced no skeletal phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Therefore, our results indicate that Ano5 is dispensable for bone homeostasis in mice, at least under unchallenged conditions, and that these animals may not present the most adequate model to study the physiological role of Anoctamin 5.
evidence.explanation: The authors' own conclusion that the mouse is not an adequate model, which is the substance of this mismatch.

evidence.snippet: Homozygous Ano5 knock-in mice (Ano5KI/KI ) replicated GDD-like skeletal features, including massive jawbones, bowing tibia, bone fragility, sclerosis, and cortical thickening of the femoral and tibial diaphysis.
evidence.explanation: The contradicting positive knock-in result, in a different GDD allele, that makes the model evidence inconsistent rather than merely negative.

evidence.snippet: Moreover, the amino acid sequence is not conserved between humans and mice at that mutation site, where Ser is mutated to Phe in humans while Ter is mutated to Phe in mice.
evidence.explanation: Supplies a specific construct-validity explanation for the negative knock-in - the mouse allele is not the homologous lesion - which converts an unexplained species discrepancy into a testable one.

evidence.snippet: however, a similar skeletal phenotype could not be produced in another study
evidence.explanation: Records the knockout-versus-knockout non-replication in the authors' own words - the sharpest form of the mismatch, since the same null genotype yields opposite bone-mass directions across laboratories. The clause immediately preceding this one in the source describes the increased BMD and bone matrix mineralization reported in the other Ano5 knockout; it is not quoted here only because an inline citation marker sits mid-sentence and would break verbatim matching.

open_questions/3.rationale:
The mouse evidence is internally inconsistent in a way that inverts the human genotype-phenotype relationship, so no mouse result about GDD mechanism can currently be transferred to human disease without argument. A p.T491F knock-in - the murine equivalent of the human p.Ser500Phe GDD allele, taken from a thoroughly characterized patient - showed no alteration of skeletal microarchitecture or mandible morphology in heterozygotes or homozygotes, assessed at two ages in males with the result confirmed in females and in an independent clone. Meanwhile Ano5 knockout mice, and a separate p.Cys360Tyr knock-in, do develop GDD-like massive jawbones, tibial bowing and diaphyseal cortical thickening.
Worse, the two null lines disagree with EACH OTHER. Wang's knockout gave osteosclerosis and hypermineralized matrix; Li's knockout gave low bone volume with defective osteoblast and osteoclast differentiation. Li et al. state the non-replication plainly. So the model evidence is not merely positive-versus-negative: three independent lines carrying ANO5 lesions produce three different skeletal directions, and two of them share a genotype. Together with the null-models-a-missense-disease problem, this means the mouse literature cannot presently arbitrate the gain- versus loss-of-function question it is most often invoked to settle. There is at least one concrete, testable explanation for the negative knock-in rather than a bare species hand-wave: Li et al. point out the residue is not conserved - the human change is Ser to Phe while the murine equivalent is Ter to Phe - so the mouse allele may simply not be the same lesion, and they also argue the animals were phenotyped too late. That is an argument about construct validity, and it is why the negative result is recorded here as a mismatch to be resolved rather than as a refutation of the human mechanism.

evidence.snippet: Here, we show that a missense mutation, p.Arg918Gln (c.2753G > A), of NLRP3 causes autosomal-dominant sensorineural hearing loss in two unrelated families.
evidence.explanation: Establishes the specific NLRP3 variant as the cause of autosomal dominant sensorineural hearing loss in the two index families.

steps/1.description: A heterozygous missense variant in NLRP3 - p.Arg918Gln (c.2753G>A) in the leucine-rich repeat domain in both originally reported families - lowers the activation threshold of the NLRP3 sensor. The same class of variant causes the cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes; what distinguishes DFNA34 is which tissue manifests the consequence, not the nature of the lesion.

evidence.snippet: The inflammasome can indeed be activated in macrophage/monocyte-like cells of the mouse cochlea, with secretion of IL-1β.
evidence.explanation: Supports the existence of a functional, activatable NLRP3 inflammasome in cochlear macrophage-like cells.

steps/2.description: Mutant NLRP3 oligomerizes and recruits ASC and pro-caspase-1 with a reduced requirement for a second activating signal. The cells that matter for this entry are the macrophage/monocyte-like cells resident in the cochlea, which express NLRP3 and carry a functional inflammasome; this was the observation that made a cochlea-only phenotype mechanistically coherent rather than merely an odd CAPS variant.

evidence.snippet: NLRP3 variants cause CAPS and DFNA34 by constitutively activating the NLRP3 inflammasome and increasing IL-1β release.
evidence.explanation: States increased IL-1 beta release as the shared consequence of the NLRP3 variants that cause DFNA34.

evidence.snippet: monocytes from three affected individuals were cultured with lipopolysaccharide and the cells secreted high levels of IL-1β compared with non-detectable levels of IL-1β secreted by healthy control monocytes.
evidence.explanation: The human functional measurement behind this node - patient monocytes secrete IL-1 beta where control monocytes secrete none - which is what makes the gain-of-function call a human observation rather than an inference from the mouse.

evidence.snippet: Monocytes from patients with CAPS only require an initial priming signal to induce IL-1β secretion, whereas wild-type control cells require a second activating signal (25).
evidence.explanation: Gives the mechanistic form of the same result - the variant removes the requirement for a second signal - which is what "constitutively activating" means at this step.

steps/3.description: Active caspase-1 cleaves pro-IL-1 beta to mature IL-1 beta, which is secreted into the cochlear microenvironment. The human evidence that the variant is functionally activating is peripheral rather than cochlear: monocytes from affected individuals secrete IL-1 beta on priming alone, where control monocytes secrete none and require a second signal. The cochlear compartment of the same step is shown only in mouse, so the inference this node makes is that the cell-autonomous defect measured in blood monocytes is the same one operating in cochlea-resident macrophages.

evidence.snippet: Interestingly, both cochlea-infiltrating and -resident macrophages contribute to peripheral inflammation-mediated hearing loss of CAPS mice.
evidence.explanation: Attributes the hearing loss to both macrophage populations, supporting infiltration as a mechanistically active step rather than a bystander finding.

evidence.snippet: On post-contrast MRI-FLAIR, pathologic enhancement of the cochlea was identified in an affected individual, similar to but less severe than that observed in the patients with NOMID or MWS.
evidence.explanation: Cochlear enhancement is the imaging correlate of barrier breakdown; it evidences the node by inference from contrast behaviour rather than by direct measurement of the barrier.

steps/4.description: IL-1 beta and downstream mediators increase permeability of the blood-labyrinth barrier, admitting circulating macrophages into cochlear tissue. In DFNA34 patients this is seen indirectly as pathologic enhancement of the cochlea on post-contrast MRI-FLAIR; in NLRP3-mutant mice it is measured directly, and both resident and infiltrating macrophages contribute to the resulting hearing loss.

evidence.snippet: The hematoxylin-eosin sections of Nlrp3 D301NneoR/+; Gfi1 Cre/+ mice cochleae at P12 exhibited a disorganized organ of Corti between the outer hair cells/supporting Deiters' cells and basilar membrane compared with the normal phenotype mice, leading to a collapsed Nuel's space.
evidence.explanation: Direct histopathologic evidence that altered Nlrp3 disorganizes the organ of Corti, the structural correlate of this node.

evidence.snippet: Speech recognition scores ranging from 60 to 100% were consistent with cochlear, but not retrocochlear, etiology.
evidence.explanation: Localizes the lesion to the cochlea rather than the auditory nerve or central pathway, which is what this node asserts.

steps/5.description: Sustained cochlear autoinflammation injures the sensory epithelium of the organ of Corti and its supporting structures, producing bilateral high-frequency-predominant loss that extends to lower frequencies with age. Human cochlear histopathology is unavailable, so the cellular detail is supplied by mouse models: conditional mutant Nlrp3 expression yields severe hearing loss with a disorganized organ of Corti.

evidence.snippet: In family LMG446, hearing loss is accompanied by autoinflammatory signs and symptoms without serologic evidence of inflammation as part of an atypical CAPS phenotype and was reversed or improved by IL-1β blockade therapy.
evidence.explanation: Documents the systemic branch in one of the two index families, including its dissociation from serologic inflammatory markers.

steps/6.description: The extracochlear branch, present in family LMG446 and absent in LMG113. Its variability at a single genotype is the unexplained part of the entry: the same p.Arg918Gln allele produced an atypical CAPS phenotype in one kindred and isolated hearing loss in the other.

evidence.snippet: DFNA34 HL has an onset during early adulthood and progresses approximately 1.2 dB/yr.
evidence.explanation: Gives the onset window and the quantitative progression rate for this phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Eight subjects had bilateral sensorineural HL with an onset in the late 2nd to 4th decade of life.
evidence.explanation: Cohort observation establishing bilateral sensorineural loss with adult onset in the index family.

steps/7.description: Bilateral, symmetric sensorineural hearing loss with onset from the late second to the fourth decade, deteriorating about 1.2 dB per year. Normal thresholds in carriers aged 16 to 32 make age-dependent penetrance part of the phenotype rather than an exception to it.

evidence.snippet: Slowly progressive HL initially primarily affected high frequencies.
evidence.explanation: States the high-frequency-predominant onset pattern.

steps/8.description: The loss begins at high frequencies with a downsloping configuration and recruits low and middle frequencies with advancing age.

evidence.snippet: Patients with CAPS and DFNA34 show progressive bilateral sensorineural hearing loss.
evidence.explanation: Review statement that DFNA34 hearing loss is bilateral and progressive.

evidence.snippet: In family LMG446, hearing loss is accompanied by autoinflammatory signs and symptoms without serologic evidence of inflammation as part of an atypical CAPS phenotype and was reversed or improved by IL-1β blockade therapy.
evidence.explanation: Records autoinflammatory signs and symptoms in the syndromic family. The quote does not enumerate fever, so this supports the sign by inference from the atypical CAPS phenotype rather than by naming it.

steps/10.description: Part of the autoinflammatory branch, and only in the syndromic subtype.

evidence.snippet: Patients with CAPS show systemic inflammatory symptoms, and hearing loss is a characteristic feature.
evidence.explanation: Supports systemic inflammatory features accompanying the hearing loss in the NLRP3 spectrum; the quote does not itself name urticaria, so this is indirect support for the specific sign.

evidence.snippet: Patients with CAPS show systemic inflammatory symptoms, and hearing loss is a characteristic feature.
evidence.explanation: As for urticaria - supports the systemic inflammatory branch generally rather than arthralgia specifically.

evidence.snippet: Gain-of-function mutations of NLRP3 result in abnormal activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome, and cause the autosomal dominant systemic autoinflammatory disease spectrum, termed cryopyrin-associated periodic syndromes (CAPS).
evidence.explanation: States the causal step from a gain-of-function NLRP3 variant to abnormal inflammasome activation, which is the edge being asserted here.

evidence.snippet: The NLRP3 inflammasome can indeed be activated in resident macrophage/monocyte-like cells in the mouse cochlea, resulting in secretion of IL-1β.
evidence.explanation: Directly reports inflammasome activation in cochlear resident macrophages producing IL-1 beta, which is this edge.

edges/3.description: The branch that is present in some carriers and absent in others. It is the same molecular lesion acting outside the cochlea.

evidence.snippet: Peripheral inflammation induced by a repetitive low dose of LPS injection caused a blood-labyrinth barrier disruption, macrophage infiltration into cochlea and cochlear inflammasome activation in an NLRP3-dependent manner.
evidence.explanation: Ties inflammasome activation to barrier disruption and macrophage infiltration, and shows the link is NLRP3-dependent.

evidence.snippet: Here, we show that a missense mutation, p.Arg918Gln (c.2753G > A), of NLRP3 causes autosomal-dominant sensorineural hearing loss in two unrelated families.
evidence.explanation: Establishes NLRP3 as the causative gene.

evidence.snippet: We identified the second DNFA34 pedigree worldwide with a novel NLRP3 variant supported by in vitro analysis.
evidence.explanation: Independent second pedigree with a different NLRP3 variant, with functional support. The source spells the locus "DNFA34"; the snippet is quoted as printed.

genes/0.notes: Encodes the inflammasome sensor cryopyrin. p.Arg918Gln (c.2753G>A) is the variant in both originally reported DFNA34 families; a second pedigree with a different NLRP3 variant was subsequently reported with in vitro support.

evidence.snippet: In family LMG446, hearing loss is accompanied by autoinflammatory signs and symptoms without serologic evidence of inflammation as part of an atypical CAPS phenotype and was reversed or improved by IL-1β blockade therapy.
evidence.explanation: Reports reversal or improvement of hearing loss under IL-1 blockade.

evidence.snippet: However, it should be noted that there is a window of opportunity to respond to treatment, and younger patients are most likely to respond.
evidence.explanation: Qualifies the treatment claim with the therapeutic window; recorded so the entry does not overstate responsiveness.

treatments/0.description: Recombinant IL-1 receptor antagonist. This is the treatment that makes the entry unusual: hearing loss was reversed or improved in affected members of the syndromic family, and improvement against natural course was seen in three probands in an independent cohort. Response is not universal - a baseline threshold worse than 60 dB and cochlear enhancement on MRI both track with poor audiologic response even when systemic symptoms settle.

evidence.snippet: Significant improvement of hearing status against the natural course, showing response to anakinra, was identified in three probands, one of whom used to have severe SNHL.
evidence.explanation: Clinical response to IL-1 receptor blockade is the therapeutic test of this mechanism node.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Blocks signalling by the IL-1 beta that the activated cochlear inflammasome secretes, rather than the inflammasome itself.

evidence.snippet: All three subjects showed excellent audiological outcomes with rapid improvement of speech perception test result reaching plateau at 3 months after CI, although distribution of the disease predicted poor outcome based on theoretical analysis.
evidence.explanation: Reports outcomes after implantation in NLRP3-related disease, one of the three subjects having DFNA34.

treatments/1.description: For hearing loss too advanced to respond to IL-1 blockade. The theoretical concern was that ubiquitous resident macrophages involving the spiral ganglion and cochlear nerve would predict poor outcomes; the reported outcomes were good.

evidence.snippet: Analyses of the variant proteins suggested that mutations negatively affect protein processing and/or function
evidence.explanation: The founding functional characterisation of the HHT5 alleles as processing defects.

evidence.snippet: Furthermore, whereas wild-type medium induced a fivefold increase in ID1 expression in cultured endothelial cells and a threefold increase in pre-miR-21, conditioned media from the mutant construct failed to upregulate these BMP-responsive target genes
evidence.explanation: Shows the processing defect is functional, not merely biochemical: mutant conditioned medium cannot activate BMP target genes in endothelium.

evidence.snippet: This protein is cleaved by subtilisin-related pro-protein convertases
evidence.explanation: Identifies the normal maturation step that the HHT5 missense alleles disrupt.

steps/1.description: BMP9 is synthesised as a precursor consisting of a prodomain and a C-terminal growth-factor domain, cleaved by furin-type proprotein convertases so that the prodomain remains non-covalently bound to the mature dimer. The two functionally characterised HHT5 missense alleles do not abolish expression of the precursor; they block this maturation step. Cells transfected with the p.Cys428Arg construct expressed the proprotein but secreted no mature BMP9 dimer, and conditioned medium from the mutant failed to induce the BMP target genes ID1 and pre-miR-21 in endothelial cells. The truncating alleles act earlier and more completely: p.Gln26Ter protein could be translated from an internal methionine but was neither processed nor secreted.

evidence.snippet: As expected, there was no detectable circulating BMP9 in the homozygotes, while the heterozygotes had circulating levels below those of healthy controls, suggesting haplosufficiency.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the node and, in the same sentence, records the dose dependence that distinguishes biallelic from monoallelic carriers.

evidence.snippet: Plasma BMP9 levels in the patients were significantly lower than controls.
evidence.explanation: Shows the same node is reached by a heterozygous processing-defective allele, not only by biallelic truncation.

evidence.snippet: The concentration of circulating BMP9 was found to vary between 2 and 12 ng/mL in sera and plasma from healthy humans, a value well above its EC(50) (50 pg/mL)
evidence.explanation: Establishes that BMP9 normally circulates far above its half-maximal effective concentration, which is why losing it is a systemic signalling loss rather than a local one.

steps/2.description: BMP9 is secreted principally by the liver and circulates in plasma; BMP10 levels track it closely, partly through circulating BMP9/BMP10 heterodimers. In children homozygous for GDF2 nonsense alleles, plasma BMP9 and BMP10 were both undetectable and serum-derived endothelial BMP activity was correspondingly low. In the heterozygous classic-HHT family, circulating BMP9 was significantly reduced rather than absent. This node is the systemic step that makes HHT5 a ligand-deficiency disease, in contrast to the receptor and co-receptor haploinsufficiencies of HHT2 and HHT1, and it is the reason plasma BMP9 is a candidate biomarker for this entity specifically.

evidence.snippet: BMP9 and BMP10 have been shown to bind directly with high affinity to ALK1 and endoglin, and BMP9 mutations have recently been linked to a vascular anomaly syndrome that has phenotypic overlap with HHT.
evidence.explanation: Establishes that the BMP9 ligand and the HHT1/HHT2 receptor proteins are partners in one complex, which is what places this node downstream of ligand loss.

evidence.snippet: Ultimately, this signaling axis is considered to maintain normal endothelial homeostasis by promoting endothelial quiescence and reducing apoptosis and barrier permeability
evidence.explanation: States the homeostatic function of the BMP9/ALK1 axis whose reduction defines this node.

steps/3.description: BMP9 and BMP10 bind a heterotetrameric endothelial receptor complex of two ALK1 type-I receptors and two type-II receptors (BMPR-II, ActR-IIA or ActR-IIB), with endoglin as co-receptor, and signal through phosphorylation of SMAD1/5/8 and complex formation with SMAD4. Loss of ligand therefore converges on exactly the pathway that ACVRL1 (ALK1, HHT2), ENG (endoglin, HHT1) and SMAD4 variants disrupt at the receptor, co-receptor and effector levels - which is the mechanistic reason a ligand disease sits inside the HHT series at all.

evidence.snippet: HHT pathogenesis strongly relies on overactivated PI3K/Akt/mTOR and VEGFR2 pathways in endothelial cells (ECs)
evidence.explanation: The primary statement of this node, from the study that established it in BMP9/BMP10-deficient and Alk1/Eng mouse models.

evidence.snippet: these results suggest that BMP-9 is a physiological ALK1 ligand that plays an important role in the regulation of angiogenesis
evidence.explanation: Supplies the upstream half of the claim: BMP9 is the physiological ALK1 ligand whose loss releases these pathways.

steps/4.description: Losing the BMP9/ALK1-SMAD1/5/8 input does not merely remove a brake; it releases two proliferative signalling arms. In HHT models, endothelial PI3K/Akt/mTOR and VEGFR2 signalling become overactivated, and correcting them pharmacologically blocks and reverses arteriovenous malformations. The reason this node belongs in a GDF2 entry rather than only in the parent disease is the model used: the malformations were produced by BMP9/BMP10 immunoblockade, which is a ligand-deficiency model and therefore the closest available experimental analogue of HHT5 itself. It is nonetheless a mouse model and not a GDF2 patient, so the node is marked PROVISIONAL. It is also the mechanistic rationale for the single reported sirolimus response in this entity.

evidence.snippet: a bmp9-deficient zebrafish model demonstrated that BMP9 is involved in angiogenesis
evidence.explanation: The only in vivo evidence tying BMP9 loss specifically to angiogenesis; model-organism data, and not on its own sufficient for the human claim.

evidence.snippet: the current working model is that BMP9 and BMP10 maintain a quiescent endothelial state that is dependent on the level of ALK1/endoglin activation in endothelial cells
evidence.explanation: States the quiescence function whose loss defines this node.

steps/5.description: The working model for the whole HHT series is that BMP9/BMP10 signalling through ALK1 and endoglin holds endothelium in a quiescent state, and that losing it re-activates angiogenesis or sensitises the endothelium to angiogenic stimuli, producing endothelial hyperproliferation and hypermigration. Direct demonstration for the GDF2 lesion specifically is animal and in vitro: a bmp9-deficient zebrafish showed BMP9 is required in angiogenesis, and mutant BMP9 conditioned medium failed to induce ID1 in cultured endothelial cells. Marked PROVISIONAL rather than ESTABLISHED because the quiescence-to-AVM step is inferred from the shared pathway and from model systems rather than observed in HHT5 patient tissue.

evidence.snippet: Although patients reported to date have manifestations that overlap with those of HHT, none meet the Curaçao criteria for HHT and seem distinct from HHT in terms of the location and appearance of telangiectases, and a tendency for tiny, diffuse PAVMs.
evidence.explanation: States how the HHT5 lesion set differs from HHT in both site and size, which is what this node's description records.

evidence.snippet: These three individuals had epistaxis and dermal lesions that were described as telangiectases but whose location and appearance resembled lesions described in some individuals with RASA1-related disorders (capillary malformation-arteriovenous malformation syndrome).
evidence.explanation: The founding description of the lesion type, explicitly distinguishing it from classic HHT telangiectasia.

steps/6.description: The tissue lesion is a direct artery-to-vein connection without an intervening capillary bed - a telangiectasis where small and superficial, an arteriovenous malformation where large or visceral. In HHT5 the reported distribution is distinctive rather than simply a milder version of HHT: the cutaneous lesions are spider-like or linear and fall on the cheeks, chin and face rather than on the lips, oral cavity and finger pads that the Curacao criteria specify, and the pulmonary lesions tend to be numerous, tiny and diffuse rather than discrete feeding-vessel AVMs. The one reported heterozygous family is the exception on the cutaneous side, with telangiectasia its authors called typical of HHT.

evidence.snippet: Genetic screening revealed a novel homozygous nonsense mutation in the BMP9 gene (c.76C > T; p.Gln26Ter). The child had no telangiectasias or arteriovenous malformations; family history also was negative.
evidence.explanation: The index case for the PAH branch, and the evidence that this branch can occur with no telangiectatic or shunting lesion at all.

evidence.snippet: The combination of increased muscularization and vasoconstriction underlies the elevated resting mean pulmonary artery pressure
evidence.explanation: Describes the remodelling process modelled by this node.

steps/7.description: A branch of the same ligand deficiency, reached by a different vascular response. Rather than shunting, the pulmonary arterioles narrow and occlude, raising pulmonary vascular resistance and loading the right ventricle. Two of the reported homozygous GDF2 children took this route: one presented at age 3 with severe pulmonary arterial hypertension and a dilated right ventricle and no evidence of a pulmonary shunt. Why the same lesion produces shunting AVMs in one child and obliterative arteriopathy in another is unexplained and is recorded as a knowledge gap.

evidence.snippet: At the age of 8 years, he developed epistaxis, and an angiogram revealed diffuse pulmonary arteriovenous malformations.
evidence.explanation: Documents diffuse pulmonary AVMs in a homozygous GDF2 proband.

evidence.snippet: The PAVMs were too small to be considered for percutaneous closure.
evidence.explanation: Records the size and treatability of the pulmonary lesions in this entity, which is what distinguishes them from typical HHT pulmonary AVMs.

evidence.snippet: He had presented at the age of 8 years with cyanosis, and was diagnosed with multiple PAVMs that were too diffuse for treatment.
evidence.explanation: The same diffuse, untreatable pulmonary phenotype in the heterozygous family.

steps/8.description: The most consistent visceral lesion in HHT5 and the reason several probands came to attention. Characteristically diffuse and small: in two independent reports the pulmonary AVMs were too tiny or too diffuse for percutaneous closure, and in one child CT pulmonary angiography showed no macroscopic lesion at all, the shunt being demonstrated only by contrast echocardiography and pulmonary angiography.

evidence.snippet: These three individuals had epistaxis and dermal lesions that were described as telangiectases but whose location and appearance resembled lesions described in some individuals with RASA1-related disorders (capillary malformation-arteriovenous malformation syndrome).
evidence.explanation: Describes the cutaneous lesions themselves - their presence, location and appearance - rather than identifying a cohort.

evidence.snippet: All three had nosebleeds and typical HHT telangiectasia, and the proband also had severe pulmonary AVMs from childhood.
evidence.explanation: The one reported family whose telangiectasia was judged typical of HHT rather than atypical.

evidence.snippet: Clinically, these patients had features resembling HHT1, including cerebrovascular involvement of their disease (first report documenting cerebral involvement of HHT5), but with earlier onset of epistaxis and a unique anatomic distribution of dermal capillary lesions that involved the upper forelimbs, trunk, and head.
evidence.explanation: Adds the third reported cutaneous pattern for this entity - dermal capillary lesions over the upper forelimbs, trunk and head - which is neither the HHT distribution nor the cheek-and-chin pattern of the homozygous cases.

steps/9.description: Spider-like or linear telangiectases, documented on the cheeks and chin in the homozygous probands, and present from early childhood - first noted at 3 years in one child. The founding report described the dermal lesions as resembling those of capillary malformation-arteriovenous malformation syndrome rather than the pinpoint lesions of HHT. The heterozygous classic-HHT family is the counterexample, with telangiectasia its authors called typical of HHT on the lips and face.

evidence.snippet: Multiple spider‐like and linear telangiectases were noted on the cheeks and chin, but not the lips or oral cavity.
evidence.explanation: Gives the exact cutaneous distribution - cheeks and chin, sparing lips and oral cavity - that this phenotype records.

steps/10.description: The characteristic HHT5 cutaneous distribution, and the point on which the entity most clearly departs from HHT: spider-like and linear lesions on the cheeks and chin, sparing the lips and oral cavity that the Curacao criteria name.

evidence.snippet: At the age of 8 years, he developed epistaxis, and an angiogram revealed diffuse pulmonary arteriovenous malformations.
evidence.explanation: Documents late-onset epistaxis in a homozygous proband.

evidence.snippet: These three individuals had epistaxis and dermal lesions that were described as telangiectases
evidence.explanation: Epistaxis in all three founding heterozygous probands.

evidence.snippet: Clinically, these patients had features resembling HHT1, including cerebrovascular involvement of their disease (first report documenting cerebral involvement of HHT5), but with earlier onset of epistaxis and a unique anatomic distribution of dermal capillary lesions that involved the upper forelimbs, trunk, and head.
evidence.explanation: Reports earlier onset of epistaxis in the GDF2 cohort than in classically reported HHT, which is the opposite of the attenuated pattern seen in the homozygous cases.

steps/11.description: Present but atypical for HHT. In the homozygous cases nosebleeds were absent or infrequent - one child had none at all, another had episodes every few months, and a third developed them only at age 8, years after his hypoxaemia was found. In the heterozygous classic-HHT family epistaxis was the presenting and criterion-satisfying feature in all three affected members.

evidence.snippet: A boy aged 5 years and 2 months presented with isolated hypoxemia.
evidence.explanation: Hypoxaemia as the isolated presenting feature of a homozygous GDF2 proband.

evidence.snippet: Pulse oxygen saturation was 84% to 89%.
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the degree of desaturation.

steps/12.description: The usual presenting abnormality in the pulmonary-AVM branch, caused by right-to-left intrapulmonary shunting rather than by any parenchymal lung disease. Room-air saturations of 84-89% in one child and 88% in another were the finding that prompted investigation; in a third, standing resting saturation was 85%.

evidence.snippet: Physical examination revealed cyanosis of nail beds and clubbed fingers.
evidence.explanation: Documents cyanosis together with digital clubbing in a homozygous proband.

steps/13.description: Follows the intrapulmonary shunt. Reported as nail-bed cyanosis in one child and as the presenting sign at age 8 in another; a third was noticed by her mother to have "blue tinged" fingers for weeks before admission.

evidence.snippet: Physical examination revealed cyanosis of nail beds and clubbed fingers.
evidence.explanation: Records clubbing in the setting of chronic desaturation.

steps/14.description: A consequence of chronic hypoxaemia from long-standing intrapulmonary shunting, reported in both the homozygous Chinese proband and the heterozygous proband with untreatable diffuse pulmonary AVMs.

evidence.snippet: he was compensating for this by polycythemia (hemoglobin 201 g/L, hematocrit 0.558)
evidence.explanation: Quantifies the compensatory erythrocytosis and states its cause.

steps/15.description: Compensatory erythrocytosis in response to chronic hypoxaemia. Reported as a haemoglobin of 201 g/L with haematocrit 0.558 in the severely shunted heterozygous proband, and as an elevated haemoglobin on admission in a homozygous child.

evidence.snippet: We report the case of a 5-year-old Hispanic boy who was diagnosed with severe PAH and right heart failure at 3 years of age.
evidence.explanation: The index paediatric PAH case with a homozygous GDF2 nonsense allele.

evidence.snippet: Mean pulmonary arterial pressure was not elevated (10 mmHg).
evidence.explanation: Shows the AVM branch runs without pulmonary hypertension, which is why the two are curated as separate phenotypes rather than as a sequence.

steps/16.description: The alternative pulmonary presentation, and the one for which GDF2 has the stronger gene-disease evidence overall. Reported in children homozygous for GDF2 nonsense alleles, severe and early: one presented at age 3 with a dilated right ventricle and estimated systolic pulmonary arterial pressure above 100 mmHg. It is a distinct branch, not a complication of the AVMs - the index PAH child had no telangiectases or AVMs at diagnosis, and the children with diffuse pulmonary AVMs had normal pulmonary artery pressures.

evidence.snippet: Clinically, these patients had features resembling HHT1, including cerebrovascular involvement of their disease (first report documenting cerebral involvement of HHT5), but with earlier onset of epistaxis and a unique anatomic distribution of dermal capillary lesions that involved the upper forelimbs, trunk, and head.
evidence.explanation: The first and so far only report of cerebral involvement in GDF2-related disease, in the authors' own words.

steps/17.description: Cerebral vascular involvement was documented for the first time in this entity in a cohort of four GDF2 probands, whose authors described their features as resembling HHT1. It is recorded here at the resolution the source supports: the abstract states cerebrovascular involvement without specifying the lesion, so the binding is to abnormal cerebral vascular morphology rather than to cerebral arteriovenous malformation. Two of the four probands carried multi-megabase 10q11 deletions, so a contiguous-gene contribution to their neurological findings cannot be excluded from the published data.

evidence.snippet: In vitro studies showed the mutant construct expressed the proprotein but lacked active mature BMP9 dimer, suggesting the mutation disrupts correct cleavage of the protein. Plasma BMP9 levels in the patients were significantly lower than controls.
evidence.explanation: Connects the processing defect measured in vitro to the reduced circulating BMP9 measured in the same patients, which is precisely this edge.

evidence.snippet: Plasma levels of both BMP9 and BMP10 were undetectable in the two homozygous index cases and this corresponded to low serum-derived endothelial BMP activity in the patients.
evidence.explanation: Directly couples absent circulating ligand to reduced BMP signalling activity measured in an endothelial reporter line - the edge itself, assayed in patient serum.

evidence.snippet: HHT pathogenesis strongly relies on overactivated PI3K/Akt/mTOR and VEGFR2 pathways in endothelial cells (ECs)
evidence.explanation: States that loss of this signalling axis leads to overactivation of these downstream pathways, which is this edge.

evidence.snippet: Intriguingly, the genes identified with deleterious mutations in HHT and PAH patients overlap considerably and collectively that suggests disruption of endothelial BMP9/10 signaling.
evidence.explanation: The published basis for running the pulmonary arterial hypertension branch off the same reduced endothelial BMP9/10 signalling node.

evidence.snippet: In accordance with this model, to explain the etiology of HHT we hypothesize that a deficient BMP9/BMP10/ALK1/endoglin pathway may lead to re-activation of angiogenesis or a greater sensitivity to an angiogenic stimulus.
evidence.explanation: States the causal step from deficient pathway activity to loss of the quiescent state. Graded OTHER because the source is a review advancing a working model rather than reporting primary data.

evidence.snippet: Resulting endothelial hyperproliferation and hypermigration may lead to vasodilatation and generation of an arteriovenous malformation (AVM).
evidence.explanation: States this specific step - from the altered endothelial cell behaviour to the vascular lesion - in the source's own hedged terms.

evidence.snippet: Our data demonstrate that Cx37 expression is differentially regulated by shear stress and SMAD1/5 signaling, and that reduced Cx37 expression is permissive for capillary enlargement into shunts.
evidence.explanation: A primary experimental result for the same step, and a stronger one than the review's working model: it identifies the effector (Cx37) whose loss permits a capillary to enlarge into a shunt.

evidence.snippet: Pathologically HHT is characterized by telangiectases and arteriovenous malformations (AVMs), the latter representing dilated tortuosities forming direct links between arteries and veins, thus bypassing the capillary bed.
evidence.explanation: States that the malformation lesion modelled by this node is what constitutes the pulmonary AVM the edge points at.

edges/9.description: The cheek-and-chin distribution reported in the biallelic cases is the superficial form of the same lesion.

evidence.snippet: Clinically, these patients had features resembling HHT1, including cerebrovascular involvement of their disease (first report documenting cerebral involvement of HHT5), but with earlier onset of epistaxis and a unique anatomic distribution of dermal capillary lesions that involved the upper forelimbs, trunk, and head.
evidence.explanation: Attributes cerebrovascular involvement to GDF2-related disease, which is what this edge asserts.

edges/10.description: Reported once, in a four-proband cohort. The edge is drawn because the cohort attributes the cerebrovascular findings to GDF2 disease, but two of those four probands carried multi-megabase 10q11 deletions, so a contiguous-gene contribution cannot be excluded from the published data.

evidence.snippet: However, the telangiectases were atypical for HHT and considered more consistent with a capillary-malformation AVM syndrome
evidence.explanation: Ties the cutaneous lesion in GDF2 patients to the malformation process this node models, while recording that its morphology differs from classic HHT.

evidence.snippet: Nosebleeds are the most common symptom in HHT and frequently lead to iron deficiency anemia.
evidence.explanation: Nosebleeds in this disease family arise from telangiectases of the nasal mucosa, so the epistaxis edge runs from the lesion node. Cited from the review framing rather than from a GDF2 case series, which is why this edge is weaker than the two above.

evidence.snippet: The pathology of PAH is characterized by narrowing and occlusion of pulmonary arterioles due to excessive proliferation and hypertrophy of cells in the vessel intima, media, and adventitia
evidence.explanation: States that the arteriolar remodelling this node models is what produces the pulmonary arterial hypertension the edge points at.

evidence.snippet: A pulmonary perfusion scan revealed radioactivity in the brain and bilateral kidney, suggesting the existence of a intrapulmonary shunt.
evidence.explanation: Demonstrates the intrapulmonary right-to-left shunt that links the malformations to systemic desaturation in this patient.

edges/14.description: Right-to-left shunting through the malformations desaturates systemic arterial blood.

edges/15.description: Visible desaturation of peripheral and nail-bed blood.

edges/16.description: Chronic desaturation remodels the nail beds and terminal phalanges.

evidence.snippet: he was compensating for this by polycythemia (hemoglobin 201 g/L, hematocrit 0.558)
evidence.explanation: States the compensatory relationship between the desaturation and the erythrocytosis.

edges/17.description: Erythropoietic compensation for chronic arterial desaturation.

evidence.snippet: These data confirm a genetic cause of a vascular-anomaly syndrome that has phenotypic overlap with HHT.
evidence.explanation: The founding assignment of GDF2 as the causal gene of this entity, stated in the authors' own careful wording.

evidence.snippet: In conclusion, we propose that this heterozygous GDF2 variant is a rare cause of HHT associated with pulmonary AVMs.
evidence.explanation: The strongest published statement that a heterozygous GDF2 allele causes HHT proper rather than an HHT-like syndrome.

evidence.snippet: With the recent expansion of population-scale whole genome sequencing (WGS), one of these variants (p.Arg333Trp) is found in 0.1% of control chromosomes, and thus its pathogenicity is now uncertain
evidence.explanation: Records the retraction in confidence for one of the three founding alleles, which is why the variant list above flags it rather than reciting it.

evidence.snippet: Twelve genes (BMPR2, ACVRL1, ATP13A3, CAV1, EIF2AK4, ENG, GDF2, KCNK3, KDR, SMAD9, SOX17, and TBX4) were classified as having definitive evidence
evidence.explanation: Supports the note that GDF2's definitive gene-disease validity was established for pulmonary arterial hypertension, not for HHT.

genes/0.notes:
Inheritance for this gene is reported both as heterozygous (autosomal dominant, the OMIM assignment) and as homozygous (biallelic, in consanguineous or founder settings); see the two inheritance blocks and the hht5_inheritance_mode discussion. Both mechanistically characterised missense alleles act by blocking cleavage of the BMP9 proprotein rather than by abolishing transcription.
Two further cautions for anyone extending this block. First, p.Arg333Trp - one of the three founding alleles - was later found at 0.1% of control chromosomes in population-scale sequencing and its pathogenicity is now uncertain; do not cite it as an established pathogenic variant. Second, GDF2 has a much better established gene-disease relationship with pulmonary arterial hypertension than with HHT: the ClinGen-style PAH gene curation classified GDF2 as definitive for heritable/idiopathic PAH, whereas no comparable definitive classification exists for GDF2-HHT, and the GeneReviews HHT chapter still confines molecular diagnosis of HHT to ACVRL1, ENG and SMAD4.

evidence.snippet: At the age of 9 years, he was treated with sirolimus, and his condition improved significantly.
evidence.explanation: The single reported treatment response in GDF2-related disease.

treatments/0.description: An mTOR inhibitor used for vascular anomalies, reported in a single homozygous GDF2 child with diffuse pulmonary AVMs that were untreatable by embolisation; his condition improved significantly after treatment was started at age 9. This is one anecdote, not an evidence base, and it is recorded because it is the only pharmacological intervention reported to have changed the course of the pulmonary lesion in this entity.

evidence.snippet: HHT pathogenesis strongly relies on overactivated PI3K/Akt/mTOR and VEGFR2 pathways in endothelial cells (ECs)
evidence.explanation: Identifies mTOR as an overactivated pathway downstream of the lesion, which is what makes sirolimus a mechanistically directed choice here rather than an empirical one.

treatments/0/targets/0.description: Sirolimus inhibits mTOR, one of the two arms shown to be overactivated downstream of lost BMP9/ALK1 signalling. In a BMP9/BMP10-immunoblockade model - the closest experimental analogue of the HHT5 lesion - mTOR inhibition combined with receptor tyrosine kinase inhibition blocked and reversed arteriovenous malformations. That is the mechanistic rationale for the single reported clinical response; it is a model result, not a demonstration in a GDF2 patient.
